article_text:
Chandigarh: Punjab Police has dismantled a sophisticated, inter-state cheating racket operating during Sunday's pharmacy officer recruitment examination, officials said.
Police have detained seven key conspirators of the racket along with 28 candidates, and seized 27 battery-operated wireless devices used for cheating, they said.
Police detected the use of pen cameras and real-time dictation during the exam conducted for recruiting pharmacy officers.
The exam centres were set up at Faridkot and Ferozepur. A candidate identified as Ayush in Ferozepur allegedly used a concealed pen camera to scan the question paper, which was sent to an accomplice, Sajan, in Bhiwani, Haryana, via WhatsApp, police said in a statement.
Sajan forwarded the question paper to another operative of the racket, Deepak, who was stationed at a makeshift control room inside the residence of Gurmeet Singh in Society Nagar, Faridkot.
From this location, key accused Manjit Singh and Deepak dictated the answers in real-time via wireless equipment to several candidates sitting inside the exam halls, the statement said.
Police investigation indicated that no leak of paper or involvement of officials has been found so far, it said.
The breach occurred entirely in real-time after the exam commenced, it said.
Preliminary investigation revealed that the mastermind behind the entire operation was Gurmeet Singh, an employee at the Sant Kabir Polytechnic College in Fazilka.
The racket charged desperate candidates exorbitant sums ranging between Rs 3.5 lakh and Rs 13 lakh to guarantee passing marks.
Several candidates had already handed over post-dated cheques as financial security to the scammers, police said.
The racket operated with corporate-level logistics, they added.
On the morning of the exam, several operatives gathered at a hotel on the Faridkot-Kotkapura Road to distribute the specialised, battery-operated wireless micro-devices to the compromised candidates, the statement said.
A total of 28 candidates have been detained across Faridkot and Ferozepur for using these devices, 27 of which have been seized by police, it said.
Police also detained seven main operators of the racket from Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab, and raids are underway to arrest the remaining members of the gang, it added.
An FIR is being registered in the case under the relevant sections of the BNS and the Information Technology Act.
The investigation conducted so far has found no official involvement or “insider” role in the matter.

title: Mumbai: Retired BEST Conductor, Relatives Duped Of ₹72 Lakh In Job Scam; Accused Offered Placements Via CM - Free Press Journal
extracted_title: Mumbai: Retired BEST Conductor, Relatives Duped Of ₹72 Lakh In Job Scam; Accused Offered Placements Via 'CM Quota'
article_text:
Mumbai: A massive job fraud case has surfaced in Jogeshwari, where a retired BEST conductor, along with his family members and acquaintances, was cheated of nearly Rs 72 lakh under the false promise of employment in reputed institutions such as the State Bank of India (SBI), Thane Municipal Corporation, and even through a so-called 'Chief Minister’s quota.'
The complainant, Mohan Jadhav, a resident of Satara district and a retired conductor from BEST’s Majas Depot, approached the Meghwadi police after realising he and his family had been deceived. According to a Lokmat Times report quoting the police, two accused, Tanaji Shilimkar and his son, Kushal, are alleged to have masterminded the fraud by issuing fake appointment letters and siphoning off large sums of money. Cops believe that the duo may have cheated several other unemployed youths in a similar manner.
How Did The Fraud Take Place?
Jadhav came into contact with Tanaji years ago when both were employed as conductors at the Majas Depot. Their families grew close over time, and after Jadhav’s retirement in March 2022, they remained in touch. When Jadhav’s elder daughter, Pooja, began searching for a job, Tanaji offered to help her, claiming he had access to placements through the Chief Minister’s quota. Trusting his long-time acquaintance, Jadhav paid him Rs 5 lakh for his daughter’s supposed posting in SBI. Soon after, the Shilimkars handed over a fake appointment letter, strengthening the family’s faith in them.

article_text:
Around 700 interns and employees have been alleged financial fraud by Thynk Technology India, an IT company operating from the Garage Imperial Rise building in Hinjawadi Phase 2.
The affected workers have claimed that the company had failed to pay salaries and stipends, issued cheques that got bounced, collected security deposits from interns and later shut its office without clearing dues.
Payments Stopped From February
According to the complainants, recruitment at the company had began at around mid-2025.
Initially, salaries and stipends were paid on time. Interns were reportedly promised a monthly stipend of Rs. 15,000, which helped the company to gain trust among the freshers and young professionals.
However the employees said: payments began to get delayed from the month of February 2026.
Audit Cited, Deadlines Missed
When salaries were not credited on the usual dates, employees approached the management.
They alleged that CEO and director Harshal Bhanudas Thakare had cited an internal audit and assured that pending payments would be cleared by the end of February.
The HR department also informed employees about the timeline through email as complainants said. However, the payments were allegedly not made.
Repeated Assurances, No Relief
Employees claimed that fresh dates were later given in March and April, including April 20, 29 and 30.
In one meeting, Thakare allegedly told employees that he needed three more months to clear all dues.
The workers said repeated assurances failed to result in actual payments.
Security Deposits, Bounced Cheques Alleged
The complainants alleged that interns were made to pay Rs. 15,000 as security deposit.
They also claimed that cheques issued after employee evaluations later bounced.
Some employees also alleged that Thakare informed the bank on 29th April that his cheques had been lost, creating hurdles in depositing them.
Complaints Filed With Police, Labour Office
The affected employees and interns approached Pune Police on 20th April.
A written complaint has also been submitted to the Deputy Labour Commissioner in Pune. Legal proceedings are now being done at different levels.
On 1st May, Thakare reportedly gave a written assurance accepting pending dues and promising payment within three months. However, employees said they have lost trust due to repeated delays.
Office Found Shut
Employees said the company’s Hinjawadi office is now closed.
They also claimed that vendors, laptop rental agencies and the office owner are owed money.
Many of the affected interns are freshers who had started their careers with the firm and are now facing financial and mental stress.

The Dharavi Police have arrested a wanted accused in connection with cheating a young man by luring him with the promise of a government job. The accused, identified as Nitin Chandrashekhar Deshmukh, was absconding in the case and is currently in police custody for further investigation.
According to police officials, Deshmukh allegedly claimed to have close ties with several political leaders and ministers in the state. He also falsely projected himself as the Nashik District Chief of the Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) faction led by Uddhav Thackeray. Police believe that his arrest may help unravel similar cases of job fraud.
The co-accused in the case, Kiran Ramdas Satpute, who is a relative of the complainant, is also named in the FIR.
The complainant, Prathamesh Bodkhe, resides in Dharavi with his family. His father works as a government security guard. In August 2024, a recruitment advertisement was issued for the post of Assistant Clerk in the Municipal Corporation. Prathamesh had applied for the post but did not appear for the examination despite receiving the hall ticket.
In January 2025, his cousin Kiran Satpute contacted him and introduced him to Nitin Deshmukh, claiming that Deshmukh was a well-connected politician with strong links in Mantralaya and could secure him a government job. Satpute also claimed that Deshmukh’s influence was such that “no one could refuse his word.”
Deshmukh allegedly assured Prathamesh that he would secure him a government job in exchange for money and promised a full refund if the job did not materialise.
During a phone conversation, when Prathamesh offered to transfer the money online, Deshmukh refused to accept payment directly into his own bank account, citing Income Tax scrutiny. Instead, he instructed the complainant to transfer the amount to different bank accounts.
Trusting the duo, Prathamesh transferred a total of ₹9.10 lakh into multiple bank accounts as directed.
In July 2025, Deshmukh allegedly demanded an additional ₹2 lakh, stating that more money was required to secure the job. When Prathamesh refused to pay, Deshmukh reportedly told him that he would not get the job and refused to return the money already paid.
The accused allegedly abused the complainant over the phone and threatened to kill him if he continued to demand a refund.
After realising he had been cheated, Prathamesh approached the Dharavi Police and lodged a complaint against both Deshmukh and Satpute.
Following verification of the complaint, police registered a case against the duo for cheating and criminal breach of trust. A search operation was launched to trace the accused.
After remaining absconding for nearly three to three-and-a-half months, Nitin Deshmukh was finally apprehended by the Dharavi Police. Further investigation is underway to determine whether he was involved in similar fraudulent schemes.

title: CBI files FIR, takes over Odisha police recruitment scam case - The Indian Express

article_text:
3 min readNov 14, 2025 02:19 AM IST 					
						First published on: Nov 13, 2025 at 04:45 PM IST 					
				
							 
			
				
After getting the central government’s approval, the CBI has registered an FIR and taken over the probe into alleged irregularities in Odisha’s police sub-inspector (SI) recruitment examination.
Officials said the central agency will investigate the “attempts, abetments and conspiracies” in connection with the alleged scam. An officer of Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) rank has been assigned to investigate the matter. The agency will soon form a team and conduct searches, said officials.
The recruitment scam came to light after an anonymous phone call on September 30 tipped off police in Odisha’s Berhampur about a possible paper leak in the examination scheduled for October 5 and 6. Based on this, police intercepted three buses carrying 114 aspirants to Hyderabad, allegedly for intensive coaching on solving the leaked question paper. The bust led the Odisha Police Recruitment Board (OPRB) to postpone the exam indefinitely, citing “unforeseen” circumstances.
Though the Crime Branch of the Odisha Police had taken up the investigation and arrested 126 people, including the 114 aspirants and the alleged mastermind of the scam, Sankar Prusty, the suspected involvement of an “organised criminal syndicate and influential persons” forced the state government to hand over the case to the CBI, officials said. Heads of private firms involved in the recruitment process have also been arrested. A local court in Berhampur recently granted bail to the 114 aspirants.
“The spread of the scam to multiple states, such as Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal, is part of the reasons why the probe has been handed over to the CBI. The Crime Branch of the Odisha Police will hand over the case files, evidence and other details of the investigations to the CBI,” said a senior police officer.
The investigation so far has revealed that the alleged syndicate involved in the scam contacted aspirants and took money from them to give them coaching on “selected questions”. The candidates had agreed to pay Rs 25 lakh each in instalments — Rs 10 lakh initially and the rest after getting some “confidential information” related to the examination. Prusty is accused of being the leader of the syndicate and is alleged to have been operating through his agents.
The CBI probe may reveal more about the influential individuals backing Prusty in the scam.
Around 1.53 lakh people had applied for 933 police sub-inspector posts, with officials saying the exam will be held once the probe concludes.

Investigators noted that the UK job arrangement also failed due to procedural objections and administrative hurdles. Despite repeated failures, the accused allegedly continued to demand money in multiple instalments, citing visa processing, documentation, and verification requirements as justification for further payments.

title: Assembly passes bill with up to 10-yr jail, Rs 1cr fine for cheating, paper leak - The Times of India
extracted_title: Odisha Assembly Enacts Tough New Law Against Exam Cheating with Heavy Penalties | Bhubaneswar News - The Times of India
article_text:
Bhubaneswar: A bill that prescribes stringent punishment, including up to 10 years of imprisonment, for organised crimes in recruitment and entrance examinations was passed by the state assembly on Friday. 
The Odisha Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024, modelled after the central Act, also mandates a hefty fine of Rs 1 crore for institutions found involved in malpractices, along with blacklisting. As per the Bill, individuals resorting to unfair means and offences will be punished with imprisonment ranging from three years to five years and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh.
Moving the Bill in the assembly, chief minister Mohan Majhi said a comprehensive state legislation was required to deal with vulnerabilities of the examination system. Impersonation, cheating, disruptions and question leaks adversely affect the prospects of millions of youth, he said. "The Bill is aimed at effectively and legally deterring persons, organised groups and institutions that indulge in various unfair means," he said.
Examinations conducted by recruitment agencies such as Odisha Public Service Commission, Odisha Staff Selection Commission, Odisha Subordinate Staff Selection Commission, Service Selection Board and Odisha Police Selection Board, among others, will be covered under the Bill. 
It will also apply to entrance examinations conducted by Odisha Joint Entrance Examination authorities.
Majhi criticised the previous BJD govt, saying there was no transparency in appointments. He said officials in charge were involved in exam paper leak rackets. "There was a scam in the appointment of assistant section officers (ASOs) in the secretariat, with jobs being sold for Rs 25 lakh to 30 lakh. Despite these activities happening under their nose, the govt remained silent. The previous govt outsourced responsibilities, pushing the future of children into darkness. Our govt is committed to integrity and fulfilling promises. We plan to create 1.5 lakh new jobs and fill all vacant positions," he said.
Opposition BJD and Congress members said the Bill had nothing new. BJD MLA Ranendra Pratap Swain said the state had copied and pasted the central Act instead of coming out with a Bill which is suitable for the state. Congress legislature party leader Rama Chandra Kadam said the Bill may not be enough to ensure transparency and fairness in examinations. "Instead of pushing it hurriedly, govt should have carried out wider consultations," he said.

BHUBANESWAR: The state Crime Branch (CB) on Friday arrested four more persons, including a woman, for their alleged involvement in the police sub-inspector (SI) recruitment scam.
The CB said that the four accused Priyadarsini Samal, T Abhimanyu Dora, Arabinda Das and Biswaranjan Behera were agents and part of the syndicate run by the key accused, Sankar Prusty, the director of Panchsoft Technologies private limited, who is still at large. In a statement issued earlier in the day, CB said that while investigating the probable leak of question paper for Combined Police Service Examination (CPSE) 2024, the investigators found out that Muna had no known sources of income, but maintained a lavish lifestyle and was staying in Bhubaneswar’s Jagamara area. Munna came under our scanner and it was established that he and Srikanta had close links with Sankar, it added.
While addressing mediapersons at the agency’s headquarters in Cuttack on the day, Director General of Crime Branch Vinaytosh Mishra said, “Sankar was running the syndicate with the assistance of Muna and Srikanta. He had planned to subvert the entire examination process, break down the government machinery and create a disbelief in the minds of the public by adopting unfair means.”
Sankar did not come into the picture directly and used his agents/middle men to reach out and lure the SI exam candidates. While he actively monitored the entire illegal operation, his agents collected original certificates and blank cheques from the aspirants on the promise of providing them SI jobs.
The middlemen had assured the candidates to return their certificates after they were selected for the job. Each candidate was asked to pay Rs 20 lakh to Rs 25 lakh for the purpose. Sikar | A cyber fraud case has been reported from Rajasthan’s Sikar district, where a man was allegedly cheated of around ₹4.07 lakh after being promised a warehouse manager job in Italy. The accused reportedly lured the victim with a lucrative offer of a ₹1.5 lakh monthly salary, gradually extracting money under different pretexts in a structured manner.
The case has been registered under the Sadar police station limits. According to the complaint filed by a man named Pankaj, he came in contact with one Shankarlal Jat from Sardarsahar during his earlier employment at a private school. The initial acquaintance later turned into regular WhatsApp communication, which was allegedly exploited for the fraud.

Trust built through social media claims of overseas recruitment
The accused Shankarlal Jat allegedly used WhatsApp and social media platforms to post messages claiming that he facilitated jobs abroad. He reportedly claimed to have contacts in countries such as Dubai, Malaysia, and Arab nations, assuring easy access to work visas and overseas employment opportunities.
Using this trust, he offered the victim a warehouse manager job in Italy. The accused claimed that the total cost for processing the job would be around ₹12.5 lakh, but assured a monthly salary of ₹1.5 lakh along with overtime benefits. Tempted by the offer, the victim agreed to proceed with the process.
Money collected in installments, fake appointment letter issued
According to the victim, the accused collected nearly ₹4 lakh in multiple installments under various pretexts. An additional ₹7,000 was taken for documentation and processing charges.
To maintain credibility, the accused sent a fake appointment letter on WhatsApp on February 10, claiming that the job had been confirmed. Based on this document, the victim was asked to visit the Italy visa application center in Delhi for further processing.
However, on March 28, the victim was suddenly informed that the job process had been stopped and could not proceed further.
Fraud exposed after verification of documents
Later, the victim grew suspicious and independently verified the documents. It was discovered that the appointment letter provided was completely fake and not issued by any official authority.
When the victim demanded a refund, the accused allegedly refused to return the money. The complaint also mentions the involvement of another individual, Rahul Soni, who is said to have assisted in executing the fraudulent scheme.
Expanding network of overseas job scams
Preliminary investigation suggests that the accused targeted unemployed youth through social media and messaging platforms. Victims were first attracted with promises of high-paying overseas jobs, followed by gradual extraction of money under the guise of processing fees and documentation expenses.
Experts note that fake job offer letters, forged visa documentation, and WhatsApp-based recruitment networks have become common tools used by organized fraud groups.
Police investigation underway
Police have registered a case and initiated an investigation into the matter. Authorities are examining digital transactions, WhatsApp chats, and bank records to determine whether more individuals are involved and to identify additional victims.

RPSC woman clerk dismissed from government service:Got job through cheating in Staff Selection Board recruitment, ranked 17th in merit
- Copy link
The Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC) has dismissed clerk grade-I Saroj Bishnoi from government service with immediate effect after finding her guilty of selection through unfair means in the Junior Assistant/Clerk Grade-II Combined Direct Recruitment Examination-2018.
The employee, who had completed nearly six years of service, was found to have violated the Rajasthan Civil Services Conduct Rules. The commission stated that her act of using unfair means to clear the examination amounts to lack of integrity and unethical conduct as a government servant, which is a clear violation of service rules.
Use of bluetooth device and alleged payment to accused
Investigations confirmed that Saroj Bishnoi used unfair means such as a Bluetooth device to clear the examination. In return, she allegedly handed over signed cheques to the main accused, Paurav Kaler, which falls under serious misconduct and corruption.
Exposure based on commission input and sogy investigation
Saroj Bishnoi was selected in the OBC category merit list, securing 17th rank in the 2018 recruitment examination conducted by the Staff Selection Board, and joined service in March 2020.
Later, based on confidential and credible information received by the commission, it was revealed that she had access to the leaked question paper prior to the examination.
Following this, the commission lodged a complaint, after which the Special Operations Group (SOG) registered an FIR and began a detailed investigation. The SOG found that the main accused Paurav Kaler, along with his associates, solved the leaked paper and provided answers to Saroj Bishnoi during the exam through a Bluetooth device.
Departmental inquiry initiated under service rules
The commission initiated a departmental inquiry under Rule 16 of the Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958. During the inquiry, the accused employee attempted to delay proceedings by citing illness, hospitalisation, and personal reasons to avoid appearance.
She also argued that departmental proceedings should be stayed until the criminal case was decided in court. However, the commission rejected this plea, citing established Supreme Court and High Court rulings that departmental inquiry and criminal proceedings can run simultaneously in the interest of administrative integrity.
High court rejects plea to stay proceedings
Saroj Bishnoi also filed a writ petition in the Rajasthan High Court (Jaipur bench) seeking a stay on departmental proceedings, citing FIR No. 35/2025 of the SOG.
Considering the seriousness of the matter, the court rejected her arguments and clarified that criminal proceedings and departmental inquiries operate in different domains. While the criminal case relates to cheating and conspiracy in the examination, the departmental proceedings relate to lack of integrity and misconduct under Rules 3 and 4.
The court held that there was no justification to stay disciplinary action in such serious cases and dismissed the stay application. Following the completion of the departmental inquiry, the commission finally dismissed Saroj Bishnoi from government service.

title: When dreams were sold: The big fish in Rajasthan's SI-exam scam pond | The Lowdown - India Today
extracted_title: When dreams were sold: The big fish in Rajasthan’s SI-exam scam pond | The Lowdown
article_text:
When dreams were sold: The big fish in Rajasthan's SI-exam scam pond | The Lowdown
The 2021 Rajasthan Sub-Inspector recruitment exam, revealed a rotten system where power, politics, and greed conspired to crush dreams. Beyond the leaked papers and fake candidates lies a deeper story about how corruption festers when oversight fails, and how justice finally struck a decisive blow—cancelling the entire exam and shattering numerous lives.
In the dark days of unemployment and the shadow of Covid, the 2021 Sub-Inspector recruitment exam in Rajasthan began as a beacon of opportunity.
Over 7.97 lakh aspirants, their dreams etched in ink and sweat, sat for the Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC) test from September 13 to 15, vying for 859 coveted posts in the police force.
But beneath the surface, a sinister web was unravelling in the shadowed corridors of Rajasthan's power elite, where ambition and greed clawed at the walls of integrity.
After what seemed to be a rigorous test of skills and endurance, the final results of the three-stage process were declared on June 1, 2023. This included the final merit list for the 859 posts, whose hard work appeared to have paid off. But, a huge scandal was waiting to tarnish images and shatter hundreds of dreams.
Scent of a Scam
Whispers of foul play echoed soon after the exams, but it was during the 2023 assembly elections that the storm broke. Reacting to accusations and rumors, the opposition BJP thundered promises of justice, accusing the ruling Congress of shielding the culprits running a recruitment scam.
In December 2023, the BJP replaced the Congress-led government. Soon it tasked the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the police with hunting down the shadows.
The probe yielded damning evidence. The scam was systemic and involved multiple layers of fraud.
The exam paper was leaked from Jaipur and sold to candidates by organised “paper mafia” networks for prices ranging from Rs 15-20 lakh per copy. External gangs, such as the Bishnoi and Kaler gangs, played a role in disseminating the materials.
Malpractices extended beyond the written test to the interview stage. Each stage costing money that totalled up to a whooping crore, according to accusations.
Dummy candidates, often educated individuals like government officials, took the exam on behalf of others. For instance, a Sub Divisional Magistrate was arrested for appearing as a proxy.
Use of Bluetooth devices for real-time assistance and mass copying inside exam halls was rampant.
Despite measures like biometric verification, CCTV, and internet shutdowns, these were poorly enforced, allowing widespread cheating.
It emerged that a nexus of RPSC selection committee members, officers, government staff, even ministers, orchestrated the scam, turning a merit-based gateway into a marketplace of corruption.
The guilty fell like a house of cards: over 125 suspects, from trainee SIs dismissed mid-service to high-profile brokers. But this was just the floating scum of the rotten pond.
A Rotten Pond of Big Fish
The arrests started with the RPSC, the selection committee that conducts all important exams in the state, including those for state administrative services.
Former member Babulal Katara was arrested in 2023 (and again in September 2024). Another former member Ramu Ram Raika was arrested in September 2024, along with his son and daughter Shobha. Raika allegedly provided the sub-inspector recruitment exam paper to his children and other trainees. At least six RPSC members have been implicated overall.
Political aides followed—Kundan Kumar Pandey, secretary to a former minister; Rajkumar Yadav, personal security to ex-CM Ashok Gehlot, and his son Bharat. Rajkumar allegedly purchased the leaked SI recruitment question paper for his son.
The Court’s Hammer
The Rajasthan High Court's blade fell sharp on August 28-29, 2025. Justice Sameer Jain (Jaipur Bench) canceled the entire 2021 SI recruitment exam, declaring all selections null and void. The court ruled that “fraud vitiates everything,” emphasising that even if some honest candidates suffered, retaining the process would legitimise corruption.
It criticised the state government for not acting despite evidence and ordered the 859 tainted vacancies to be merged with 1,015 new vacancies for a fresh 2025 recruitment.
The ruling overrode a July 2025 government subcommittee report (led by Law Minister Jogaram Patel) that recommended against cancellation, arguing for segregating tainted candidates.
The court also took suo motu cognizance of RPSC members' roles and referred it to a Division Bench for further scrutiny.
Justice Sameer Jain declared: fraud voids all, even if the innocent pay for it, sanctity has to be maintained, integrity has to be restored.
Poetic Justice: Kumar Vishwas’ Wife Falls
At the heart of this labyrinth stood Manju Sharma, wife of poet and former AAP leader Kumar Vishwas. Sharma was appointed RPSC member in October 2020 under the Congress regime. She oversaw the tainted process, where interviews were prejudiced and leaks flowed like hidden rivers.
Yet, no direct accusations pierced her armor—no police probe named her, no evidence tied her hands to the leaks. As others fell, she continued to float.
In the aftermath of the court’s verdict, the conscience of the poet’s wife stirred. She resigned: “I have spent my life in transparency," her letter said, citing moral grounds amid the storm's stain on her reputation and the commission's dignity.
Was it a noble retreat or a calculated evasion? Political winds whispered of BJP pressure.
The scam's ghosts still haunt Rajasthan's halls. BJP ministers like Kirodi Lal Meena hail the purge, vowing to shield the youth from the mafia's grip.
“The paper leak mafia has destroyed many innocent lives in our state. We are with students and their interests.” Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma highlighted his government's crackdown on recruitment frauds. But the decision has left many aspirants in shock, with successful 2021 candidates paying the price of the systemic rot. They are eligible to reapply but face uncertainty.
In this thriller of betrayal, where lines between guardian and gatekeeper blur, one truth endures: corruption's roots run deep, and the next leak may already be dripping in the dark.
Timeline of Key Events
September 13-15, 2021: Exam conducted; initial leak allegations emerge.
December 2023: BJP government forms; SIT established.
February 2024: Scandal fully surfaces; SOG arrests begin.
September 2024: RPSC members, including Ramu Ram Raika and family arrested; more trainee SIs detained.
April-July 2025: Arrests of dummies, political aides, and relatives.
July 2025: Government decides against cancellation.
August 28-29, 2025: High Court cancels the exam.
September 1, 2025: RPSC member Manju Sharma, wife of poet Kumar Vishwas, resigns.

title: Rajasthan HC cancels 2021 SI recruitment exam over paper leak allegations — ‘Fraud vitiates everything’ - The Indian Express
extracted_title: Rajasthan HC cancels 2021 SI recruitment exam over paper leak allegations — ‘Fraud vitiates everything’
article_text:
4 min readJaipurAug 29, 2025 03:25 AM IST 					
						First published on: Aug 28, 2025 at 02:11 PM IST 					
				
							 
			
				
The Rajasthan High Court cancelled the Sub-Inspector Recruitment Examination, 2021, Thursday after finding large scale irregularities in the process.
This comes over a month after a six-member sub-committee of the Rajasthan government submitted a detailed report claiming that it would be “premature” to cancel the exam when investigations were still ongoing.
A single-judge bench of Justice Sameer Jain that delivered the ruling said that then members of the RPSC – including Babulal Katara and Ramu Ram Raika — were “directly involved” in leaking papers and answer keys before the exams. Both Katara and Raika are arrested – the former in 2023 and the latter in September 2024.
According to the court, the scam was not confined to the written test and that “even the interview stage was manipulated”. “Apart from this, external gangs such as the Bishnoi and Kaler gangs were engaged in distributing leaked papers,” the court said.
Investigation, the court said, had also found malpractices such as dummy candidates, Bluetooth-enabled cheating, and copying inside exam halls.
“Security measures such as biometric verification, CCTV surveillance and internet shutdowns were either poorly implemented or ignored, making it easier for cheating to spread widely,” he said. “Committees formed by the government and the Special Investigation Team (SIT) confirmed that the fraud was systemic and that it was practically impossible to separate genuine candidates from those who benefited from corruption.”
Sub-Inspector recruitment “is a highly-sensitive matter linked with law and order, and allowing such tainted recruitment to stand would destroy public trust in the police force”. “Fraud vitiates everything. Even if some honest candidates suffer, retaining the recruitment would mean legitimising large-scale corruption. In the Court’s view, the process was so tainted from within that no fair segregation of candidates was possible,” the Bench said, adding that the only “just and fair solution was to scrap the entire SI Recruitment Examination, 2021”.
A major flashpoint between the BJP and the Congress in Rajasthan, the allegations pertain to the RPSC’s 2021 recruitment exam for 859 sub-inspector and platoon commander posts.
This is the first time that an exam has been cancelled following paper leak allegations since the current Bhajan Lal Sharna government came to power in December 2023.
After the allegations surfaced in 2021, the then Congress government handed over the investigation to Special Operations Group (SOG) of the Rajasthan Police. Over 50 trainee sub-inspectors, among others, have been arrested so far.
In 2024, the Rajasthan government formed a Cabinet sub-committee to decide whether to cancel the exam. In its report submitted to the high court in July, the sub-committee led by Rajasthan’s Law Minister Jogaram Patel had recommended that the exams should not be cancelled.
“The SIT is doing a detailed investigation and making arrests. It is possible to segregate tainted and untainted candidates,” Additional Advocate General Vigyan Shah told reporters outside the court.
After the ruling, Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore refused to comment, saying it was “too soon to say anything”. “The party will consult legal experts before making any decisions,” he said.
Meanwhile, Cabinet Minister Kirodi Lal Meena claimed he had been “fighting against the paper leak mafia since the beginning”.
“I’ve sent a letter to Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma to cancel the exam. The paper leak mafia has destroyed many innocent lives in our state. We are with students and their interests,” Meena told The Indian Express.

Rajasthan woman gets railway job, leaves husband; he exposes Rs 15 lakh proxy scam
A railway employee in Rajasthan was suspended after her husband alleged a proxy candidate took her recruitment exam. Authorities are investigating the fraud, with the CBI registering a case against her and the alleged proxy candidate.
A railway employee in Rajasthan has been suspended after her husband alleged that a proxy candidate took an examination on her behalf, triggering an investigation by the authorities.
Sapna Meena, who worked as a pointsman at Sogaria railway station in Kota, was suspended following complaints from her husband, Manish Meena. "The matter is being investigated," said Saurabh Jain, Senior Divisional Commercial Officer, Kota Division.
Manish said he supported his wife’s education and helped her prepare for the railway recruitment examination. He alleged that a relative, Chetanram, arranged for a proxy candidate in exchange for Rs 15 lakh. Manish claimed he mortgaged land to finance the arrangement and that a railway employee, Rajendra, acted as an agent in the process. The proxy candidate, identified as Lakshmi Meena, allegedly took the exam on Sapna’s behalf, securing her the job.
According to Manish, Sapna left him six months after securing the job, telling him she could not stay with an unemployed person. He alleged that when he confronted Chetanram, he was deceived again, paying an additional Rs 9 lakh for a job that never materialised.
Manish later filed complaints with the vigilance department of the West Central Railway and the Central Bureau of Investigation. Authorities conducted searches in Karauli, Kota, and Alwar, seizing documents related to the case. Investigators found that a fraudulent photograph and identity were used in Sapna’s recruitment process.
The CBI has registered a case against Sapna and the alleged proxy candidate. The investigation is ongoing.

title: Rajasthan: Cheating, Paper Leaks in Govt Exams Put Aspirants’ Lives at Stake - TheWire.in
extracted_title: Rajasthan: Cheating, Paper Leaks in Govt Exams Put Aspirants’ Lives at Stake
article_text:
Jaipur: “My father wanted me to become a government officer. I tried my best all these years, exhausting all his savings on coaching classes for my competitive exam. But I never knew that the government and luck would go against me,” said 26-year-old Gopal Saraswat.
Saraswat, who appeared for examinations meant to fill Rajasthan sub-inspector (SI) and Rajasthan junior engineer (JEN) posts, just got to know of the paper leak.
He appeared for three exams in the past few years, including for the post of librarian which was cancelled due to a paper leak. On the other hand, the demand for the cancellation of the other two remains strong.
A controversy erupted after reports emerged of irregularities and paper leaks in JEN exams conducted in November 2020, and of SI and Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers (REET) exams conducted in September 2021.
Seventeen people, including the principal of a private school, were arrested in Bikaner and Jaipur over their alleged involvement in the cheating for the SI exam.
However, a major backlash against the government was witnessed with REET’s fiasco even after the state government had made elaborate security arrangements.
REET exam row
Conducted in over 4,000 centres on September 26, REET 2021 saw more than 16.5 lakh candidates apply for 31,000 posts in government schools. It is a mandatory exam for becoming a teacher in government schools. The state government provided travel facilities for the REET aspirants, including free buses and other public transport.
Chief minister Ashok Gehlot himself conducted a high-profile meeting and warned government employees of dismissing from service if they were found complicit in cheating, or malpractices. Special arrangements were made to keep a check on cheating, as various reports emerged from across the state from September 26.
“Firstly, what was the need to conduct such a big examination in one go. It could have been done in parts or in a phased manner as it happens with other exams. It would have made things easy,” said retired IAS officer and former secretary of Rajasthan Public Service Commission Rajendra Bhanawat.
Fearing for their future, aspirants across the state were distressed after news of the paper leak emerged. Hundreds of aspirants staged a protest for three days at the Shaheed Smarak in Jaipur and asked the government to re-conduct the examinations.
A call for a protest to be held on September 30 was given by the social activist and president of Rajasthan Ekikrat Berozgaar Mahasangh, Upen Yadav. However, he was arrested on that morning outside his house as he made his way to the protest site. He was released at around 5 pm.
Meanwhile, BJP MP Kirodi Meena was quick to take over the protests and asked leaders of other parties and MLAs to join. He sat with aspirants for three days before the exam was postponed on October 3 to a later day.
Meena said, “We will protest again in the future along with all BJP MLAs.” This development came after a meeting was held at BJP state headquarters on October 2, in the presence of state BJP chief Satish Poonia, Meena and other leaders.
“BJP hijacked my protest after I went to jail. I never called any political leader since it was a student protest,” Yadav told The Wire.
Before the exam, a series of important arrests were also made by the police to prevent cheating in exams.
To prevent cheating in the REET exam, the government shut down Internet in India’s largest state by area, which is home to over 68 million people. This had caused disruption in online classes for students while also affecting those working from home. The REET aspirants also faced problems in reaching their exam centres and many faced issues regarding digital payments.
According to a February 2021 report published by digital advocacy firm Internet Freedom Foundation, with 72 documented internet shutdowns since 2012, Rajasthan has witnessed the second-highest number of internet shutdowns in India after Jammu and Kashmir. The report also accused the state government of violating internet shutdown laws.
Government’s efforts in vain
Aspirants in Rajasthan have been suffering for too long because of exams being cancelled, following irregularities. Nearly three big exams have been called off in the last few years, including for the posts of junior engineer, jail warder and librarian. While jail warder posts saw six lakh applicants for as few as 925 posts, the latter saw 87,459 applicants for 700 posts.
Despite necessary arrangements, reports of various instances of cheating emerged in the REET exam. In one such case, the police busted a racket attempting to cheat using a Bluetooth and mobile phone fitted in ‘chappals’. The ‘cheating chappals’ were procured for Rs 30,000 and were sold to aspirants for more than Rs 5 lakh. Police have arrested a few people, but the main accused Tuljaram Jat is absconding. Such cases were reported in Bikaner, Pratapgarh, Ajmer and Sikar.
However, the major embarrassment for the government came when the paper was leaked even before the internet was suspended.
According to several reports by Dainik Bhaskar, nearly one-and-a-half hours prior to the commencement of the exam, at 10 am, a constable named Devendra from Gangapur city in the Sawaimadhopur district had received the question paper on his phone. Batti Lal Meena alias Vikas Meena, who had got the paper, sent the solved question paper to a person named Ashish, on WhatsApp.
Both of Ashish’s sisters were to appear for the exam. However, Ashish couldn’t forward it to them due to the internet suspension. Then he called police constable Devendra, whose wife was to take the exam as well, to meet. Devendra took a photo of the paper from Ashish’s phone and informed head constable Yudhveer, whose wife was also an applicant. Both constables were suspended later.
The state suspended 20 government employees, including one Rajasthan Administrative Service (RAS) officer, two Rajasthan Police Service (RPS) officers, one district education officer (DEO), 12 teachers, and three police personnel.
“That REET is an exam is a total fraud. The state government is responsible for it because the chief minister and chief secretary were monitoring everything. Nothing was in control of the Secondary Board of Education which was conducting the exam,” senior BJP leader and former minister Arun Chaturvedi told The Wire.
During the exam, police also arrested several dummy candidates and gangs who facilitated cheating in different districts, according to officials. Most of the suspended employees are from the Sawaimadhopur district. Despite a dozen arrests, the police could not explain how the paper was leaked.
“It does not speak well of the government’s measures. There were some lacunae which the government has not been able to plug over the years. The complete system is failing, and there is a need to improve it,” said Jaipur-based senior journalist Anil Sharma. “Over the years, in all big examinations in Rajasthan, the government has failed in its responsibility.”
Political links of the mastermind
Numerous reports suggest that Batti Lal Meena alias Vikas Meena is the mastermind behind the REET cheating scam, but the police have not been able to nab him yet. Meena’s pictures with both BJP and Congress politicians, including the education minister and state Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasara, are doing rounds on social media.
Talking to reporters on October 2, Dotasara said, “Whether it is Batti Lal or anyone, we are ready to probe everything transparently. But first, they (BJP) should give us some proof of the paper leak or irregularities or cheating. They are just diverting students who neither studied well nor done the exam well.”
While in a press conference on September 3, Special Operations Group additional director general Ashok Rathod said, “We will expose the whole paper leak racket that has seen the arrest of a total of 10 people. Battilal’s brother Rajesh has been arrested from Madhya Pradesh and raids are being conducted to nab him too.”
According to Batti Lal Meena’s Facebook page, he is a resident of Sawaimadhopur district and identifies himself as a Congress leader. He campaigned for Congress candidates in local elections and often took part in National Students Union of India (NSUI) programmes. His pictures with various public figures include Om Birla and Kirodi Meena of the BJP to Congress leaders Sachin Pilot and Srinivas B.V. He is also photographed with state NSUI chief Abhishek Poonia and Rajasthan Public Service Commission (RPSC) chairman Bhupendra Yadav.
MP Kirodi, who was pictured with Meena, told The Wire, “I don’t know him. Even I am demanding his arrest. He might have taken the photo with me in the crowd.”
According to sources, he paid visits to Dotasara’s office, along with state Congress secretary Desh Raj Meena, whose brother Kulraj Meena is posted as sub-divisional magistrate at Laxmangarh, the hometown of the education minister.
The BJP has demanded the arrest of mastermind Batti Lal Meena, a CBI inquiry and the resignation of Dotasara. It further stated that chief minister Ashok Gehlot should sack Dotasara if he fails to resign.
BJP leaders Vasundhra Raje, Gajendra Singh Singh Shekhawat, Satish Poonia, among others slammed the government over the issue and accused it of corruption. Various hashtags such as #GehlotWeak_PaperLeak, #भ्रष्ट_शिक्षामंत्री_डोटासरा, #REET_JEN_SI_परीक्षा_रद्द_करो among others trended on Twitter.
A petition was filed by a REET candidate before the Rajasthan high court requesting a Central to probe into the matter and cancel the exam. It also accused the Rajasthan government of alleged involvement. The petitioner Bhagchand Sharma is from Jaipur and is unemployed. However, he has MSc, BEd degrees along with others.
Speaking to news agency ANI on Monday, October 4, chief minister Ashok Gehlot said, “The state government managed the entire REET process very well. The news of the paper being circulated… whether the Congress or the BJP is in power, action will be taken in the REET matter.”
RAS exam controversy
The Congress government in the state was also embroiled in the controversy of the RAS exams, when education minister Dotasara was accused of favouritism during the 2016 and 2018 exams.
Dotasara’s daughter-in-law’s brother Gaurav and sister Prabha scored 80 out of 100 marks in the interview round of RAS 2018. However, in the written examination, Gaurav and Prabha secured only 49.75% and 47.44% respectively. Their scores raised suspicion, since only six applicants among the top 16 had secured 80 or more, including topper Mukta Rao, who secured 77 marks.
Dotasara’s daughter-in-law Pratibha herself cleared the RAS 2016 with 50.25% in the written exam and 80 in the interview. His son Avinash had also cleared the exam in the same year with 86 marks in the interview.
“It isn’t a coincidence for sure that all the three relatives of the education minister got 80 marks in the interview. REET also comes under him,” said Arun Chaturvedi.
These allegations emerged in the backdrop of the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) busting a RAS bribing scandal.
Apart from this, three, including the principal of a government institution, were also arrested for irregularities.
Accusations against Rajasthan PSC
The arrests and allegations relating to the RAS exam shed the spotlight on the RPSC, which conducts most of the government exams in the state. The board members of RPSC interview candidates during RAS exams.
Appointments of individuals with a political background are a common feature at the RPSC, with former bureaucrats, their relatives and political leaders making it to the board. Apart from the chairman, there are seven members on the board.
Currently, the chairman of the RPSC board is Bhupendra Yadav, who was appointed soon after taking voluntary retirement as the director general of police (DGP). The other members on the panel include Sangeeta Arya, Manju Sharma, Jaswant Singh Rathi, Shiv Singh Rathore, Rajkumari Gurjar, Babulal Katara and Ramu Ram Raika.
Sangeeta Arya is the wife of chief secretary Niranjan Arya, and she unsuccessfully contested the 2013 assembly elections from the Sojat seat on a Congress ticket. Manju Sharma is a lecturer and the wife of poet and former Aam Admi Party leader Kumar Vishwas. Rajkumari Gurjar had served as the state vice president of the BJP Mahila Morcha and is the daughter of former MLA Umrao Singh Gurjar.
The name of Rajkumari Gurjar and her husband, former IPS Bheru Singh Gurjar, had surfaced in an RPSC bribery case in July this year. While Jaswant Singh Rathi is a senior journalist, Shiv Singh Rathore, Babulal Katara and Ramu Ram Raika are academicians.
Former Rajasthan education secretary Rajendra Bhanawat told The Wire, “We have seen this in the past too, that most members aren’t appointed to the RPSC because of their merit or calibre, but due to their political affiliations. If you appoint people of calibre and merit in RPSC, the overall quality of selection and interview will certainly go up.”
Rajasthan ranked second in the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)’s report on crime in India 2020, in which 664 cases were filed in the state under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Rajasthan was also ranked the most corrupt state by the India Corruption Survey conducted by Transparency International India.
All the activists, journalists, politicians and experts that The Wire spoke to for this story, reiterated that this can’t happen without the involvement of someone from within the system; the exam could have been conducted in a phased manner and a strict law against cheating should be introduced.
Rising unemployment in the state
According to a report published by India Spend in 2019, an aspirant spends an average of three years and three months preparing for competitive exams. However, according to their qualitative findings, this number hugely underrepresents the time usually invested by those vying for government jobs. The average annual expenditure of an individual preparing for a competitive exam in Jaipur is Rs 1,95,130 with 57% of them belonging to the lower-income group (monthly family income less than Rs 20,0000).
Government jobs have always been sought-after, but given the loopholes in the system, the future of lakhs of aspirants is at stake. According to the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE)’s monthly data, Rajasthan’s rate of unemployment spiked to 53.5% during the lockdown period from May 2020 to October 2020. Their latest report suggests that Rajasthan has the second-highest unemployment rate in India, at 26.7%.
“It is a crime against the youth of the country that you can’t even hold a single exam without either any flaws or problems. What could be more traumatic for hundreds of aspirants than exams being cancelled time and again,” said Bhanawat.
The high number of youth applying for low-grade jobs in the government departments represents Indians’ obsession with government jobs, on one hand, and India’s incapability to produce enough opportunities for its qualified youth, on the other.
Referring to the 25 million people that applied for low-grade jobs in the Indian Railways, former RBI governor Raghu Rajan said in an interview to NDTV in 2019, “This is a reflection of the fact that we have a real job problem. Despite 7% growth, it is not producing jobs.”
However, for a large number of students in Rajasthan who aim to become Indian Administrative Service officers, the job of a government teacher or librarian comes as a backup option, which provides financial stability, and also because the teaching jobs give them time for self-study, unlike others.
Twenty-one-year-old REET applicant Karan Singh said, “My ultimate goal is to become an IAS officer. Teaching is not my life. Being a government teacher, I can prepare properly by even earning some money.”
It is also the same story of Gopal Saraswat, who after his father’s death had decided to become a government officer by first getting “any grade government job”. But the future of Karan, Giri and lakhs of other aspirants are left in a lurch as the government is struggling to hold at least one exam smoothly without any controversy.
Devendra Pratap Singh Shekhawat is a journalist based in Rajasthan.

title: 'Earn money from home', fraudsters misuse work-from-home scheme: Woman loses lakhs after clicking fake job ... - Bhaskar English
extracted_title: 'Earn money from home', fraudsters misuse work-from-home scheme: Woman loses lakhs after clicking fake job link; here's how to apply safely for official Rajasthan WFH scheme - Rajasthan News
article_text:
- English News
- Local
- Rajasthan
- 'Earn Money From Home', Fraudsters Misuse Work from home Scheme
'Earn money from home', fraudsters misuse work-from-home scheme:Woman loses lakhs after clicking fake job link; here's how to apply safely for official Rajasthan WFH scheme
- Copy link
The Rajasthan government's "Chief Minister Work From Home–Job Work Scheme" is under the radar of cybercriminals.
They are especially targeting women who are less familiar with digital platforms by offering them fake work-from-home job opportunities, leading to financial loss and distress.
Fraudsters are using fake messages and websites to cheat women by misusing the name of a scheme.
The scheme was launched in 2022 by the Women and Child Development Department (WCDD) of Rajasthan to give women a chance to earn from home. It promises flexible work and minimum monthly earnings of Rs 5,500, with job types ranging from data entry, designing, tailoring, packing, social media management, and other skill-based roles. While the real scheme has benefited thousands of women, fraudsters are now creating fake websites, WhatsApp groups, and Telegram channels to trick women into sharing personal details and bank information.
Real stories of fraud victims
Tamanna, a 25-year-old woman from Jaipur, became a victim of such cyber fraud. She came across a WhatsApp message offering part-time work under the Chief Minister Work From Home scheme. Curious about the opportunity, she clicked the link which led her to a Telegram group. There, a woman who introduced herself as ‘Riya Kochawa’ claimed she was from a reputed company and offered Tamanna work that could be done online from home.
“She kept guiding me and asked me to complete small online tasks to earn money. Initially, it looked real. Then she asked for my bank details for payment, and I followed her instructions. But soon, I found that over Rs 9.25 lakh had been taken from my account,” Tamanna said. She later lodged a complaint at Bajaj Nagar police station and has warned others to stay away from such groups. “The woman on Telegram made everything look genuine. I had no idea it was a scam until it was too late.”
In another case, Priya, 35, a tailoring worker from Bharatpur, was approached by a caller who claimed she could get a government job from home through the CM Work From Home scheme. “She said all I had to do was fill a form online and submit ID proof. I was about to apply but luckily an e-Mitra operator I know warned me that it was a scam,” said Priya. “Had he not informed me, I could have lost money too.”
Anisha, 23, who lives in the Jamdoli area of Jaipur, also got trapped. She clicked on a fake government website that mimicked the official one and entered her personal details. Soon after, she started receiving suspicious calls asking for OTPs and bank details. “I panicked and even received messages threatening to freeze my bank account. I had to change my phone number to stop the harassment,” she said.
Fake websites and channels
The official government website for the scheme is https://wfh.rajasthan.gov.in. However, fraudsters are circulating fake websites with similar names and designs, tricking users into thinking they are applying for government jobs.
The WCDD has made it clear that the government does not send messages through WhatsApp or Telegram, and no payment or deposit is required to register or apply under the scheme.
Government takes steps to protect women
Vijayshree Chotia, the nodal officer for the scheme, confirmed that many cases of fraud have come to their notice. “We are working with cybercrime authorities to take action against these scammers. To raise awareness, we are producing short digital awareness videos in Hindi and local dialects,” she said.
She added that women are encouraged to contact the official landline numbers for any clarification before sharing personal information online. “We have set up helpline numbers so that women can confirm details of the scheme. Our district-level officers are also conducting workshops and visiting self-help groups to provide correct information.”
The helpline number for support is 141-2716418.
How to protect yourself
- Register only on the official website https://wfh.rajasthan.gov.in.
- Never click on unknown links shared on WhatsApp or Telegram.
- Do not share OTPs, bank details, Aadhaar number, or PAN card through messages or calls.
- Be cautious of anyone who demands money or asks you to install third-party apps.
- Report fraud immediately to the police or cybercrime helpline.
About the scheme
The ‘Mukhyamantri Work From Home–Job Work Yojana’ was launched with the aim of providing employment to 20,000 women annually. Eligible women include those above 18 years of age, with at least a 12th standard education and basic computer knowledge. The scheme gives preference to widows, divorced women, and women from economically weaker sections. Jobs are assigned based on their skills and the availability of work in the private sector or through government support.
Women enrolled in the scheme receive training, and their payments are deposited directly into their bank accounts. “This scheme is an opportunity for women to become self-reliant, especially in rural areas where job opportunities are limited,” said Chotia.
As cyber fraud increases, the government has asked women to remain careful and not fall for attractive job offers shared via unofficial channels. While the scheme is real and helpful, women must verify every detail and avoid giving out sensitive information online.
For any help regarding the scheme, visit the official website or call the helpline number.

title: Massive PTI recruitment scam in Rajasthan: Over 100 hired with fake degrees in 2018, SOG expands probe - Bhaskar English
extracted_title: Massive PTI recruitment scam in Rajasthan: Over 100 hired with fake degrees in 2018, SOG expands probe - Jaipur News
article_text:
- English News

- Massive PTI Recruitment Scam In Rajasthan Over 100 Hired With Fake Degrees, SOG Expands Probe
ExclusiveMassive PTI recruitment scam in Rajasthan:Over 100 hired with fake degrees in 2018, SOG expands probe
- Copy link
Rajasthan's Special Operations Group (SOG) has uncovered large-scale fraud in both the 2018 and 2022 PTI (Physical Training Instructor) recruitments, with over 100 candidates securing jobs using fake degrees. The investigation initially focused on the 2022 recruitment, has now expanded to 2018, revealing widespread irregularities in the verification process.
Fraudulent appointments in 2018 recruitment
- In 2018, 4,655 PTI posts were filled, but physical verification of degrees was not conducted.
- Most verifications were done via correspondence, relying solely on responses from universities without proper scrutiny.
- The OPJS University in Churu, which only received recognition for B.P.Ed courses in 2016, issued degrees with backdated certificates to candidates appointed in 2018.
- More than 100 candidates were found to have used such fake degrees and have been working for five years.
Lack of proper verification
- Degree verification during the joining process was weak, allowing candidates with pre-2016 degrees from OPJS University to secure jobs despite the university not being authorized to offer the course at that time.
- Irregularities in documents included: Discrepancies in names, roll numbers, and enrollment details.Mark sheets without roll numbers or result dates.Mismatched online and offline records.Unauthorized age relaxations given to out-of-state candidates.
SOG expands probe & identifies fake PTIs
- SOG has begun calling fraudulent PTIs for questioning.
- The majority of these fake degree holders are serving in TSP areas, particularly in Dungarpur and Banswara.
- The Education Department and Selection Board are providing their records for further verification.
Fraud in 2022 PTI Recruitment & OPJS University’s Role
- The 2022 PTI recruitment fraud first exposed OPJS University's fake degree racket.
- Thousands of backdated B.P.Ed degrees were issued fraudulently.
- A SOG raid on OPJS in June 2024 led to the seizure of documents, including evidence of similar fraud in 2018.
- 141 candidates have been identified as having fake degrees—51 confirmed as forged, while 90 others were found suspicious.
Fake degree holders paid fees in cash
- Legitimate students paid fees online or via demand draft, but those obtaining fake degrees paid in cash.
- OPJS University was allocated only 100 B.P.Ed seats annually, yet thousands of degrees were issued fraudulently.
SOG’s action & government’s response
- The SOG has written to the Education Director, RPSC, and Selection Board questioning why strict verification was done in 2022 but not in 2018.
- It was found that fake degree holders either used dummy candidates or cheated in exams to pass.
- The government is now preparing to file cases against those involved.
Investigation Ongoing
SOG officials confirm that many more names are coming up as the probe continues. ADG VK Singh stated that OPJS University was the primary hub of fraud, distributing thousands of backdated B.P.Ed degrees. Authorities are now working to identify and take action against all those who secured government jobs using fake credentials.

title: Jaipur Police busts fake recruitment racket: Transport Businessman turned ‘IAS Officer’ runs fraud job rack... - Bhaskar English
extracted_title: Jaipur Police busts fake recruitment racket: Transport Businessman turned ‘IAS Officer’ runs fraud job racket, caught in Agra; 14 youths tricked with interviews, medical tests in hotels - Jaipur News
article_text:
- English News
- Local
- Rajasthan
- Jaipur
- Jaipur Police Busts Fake Recruitment Racket, Mastermind Posed As IAS Officer
ExclusiveJaipur Police busts fake recruitment racket:Transport Businessman turned ‘IAS Officer’ runs fraud job racket, caught in Agra; 14 youths tricked with interviews, medical tests in hotels
- Copy link
In Rajasthan, 14 youths were cheated in the name of government jobs by conducting fake recruitment. Murlipura police in Jaipur have arrested the mastermind of the gang. This fraudster, who runs a transport business, posed as a fake IAS officer and conducted interviews of the victim youths.
There are 6 people involved in the gang. Each was assigned different tasks. Among them, 2 accused would meet the victims posing as fake IAS officers. They would call them for interviews at expensive hotels. One gang member, posing as a doctor, would also conduct their medical examinations.
The entire fraud was executed in the style of Akshay Kumar's film 'Special-26'. The accused carried out the whole process from fake call letters to interviews in such a way that the victims had no suspicion. Dainik Bhaskar tried to understand the entire case by speaking with the police and victims' families.
First, the story of fraud
The first case against the gang was registered by retired army officer Mansingh at Murlipura police station on July 2, 2023. In this case, 2 fraudsters of the gang had already been caught. The third mastermind was arrested on March 20. During interrogation, it was revealed that the gang targeted people who wanted to get government jobs for their children by paying money.
The complainant, Mansingh's younger brother, was preparing for a government job. He came in contact with Anil Kumar Meena, former councilor of Bagru. Anil Kumar told Mansingh that his acquaintance Abhishek Sharma has connections with senior officials and ministers. Currently there are 58 posts vacant, and all these recruitments are to happen under him. Falling for the deception, many of Mansingh's relatives also agreed to get government jobs for their unemployed sons.
How they deceived: Promise of job in 6 months
Complainant Mansingh said that former councilor Anil arranged a meeting with Abhishek Sharma. He claimed that he is the PA of IAS RK Agarwal (Deepak Jain) posted in the Assembly. Their group directly recruits for Assembly LDC, Rajasthan High Court Group D, Railway, BDO, Patwari etc positions.
Currently, 58 posts are under direct recruitment through them only. According to Mansingh, the fraudster Abhishek claimed that he had already helped many people get jobs. He promised government job placement within 6 months for a deal of 6 lakh rupees.
Meetings near government offices to commit fraud
Lawyer Anil Kumar Taylor said that to build trust, the accused would often meet near the Secretariat, Assembly, and Central Park. The first meeting of the victims with fake IAS RK Agarwal was also arranged outside the Secretariat.
RK Agarwal would arrive in a shiny car just like an IAS officer. He would speak very little himself. He would mostly give instructions while sitting in the car. Other gang members would join him pretending to be his government PA and staff.
More than 6 people in fraud company, 2 posed as IAS, one as fake doctor
The gang includes more than 6 people. Each person had a different assigned role. Gang members never called each other by their real names in front of victims. The accused only took cash payments. They only communicated with victims through WhatsApp calls.
The accused convinced Mansingh that the jobs of 58 young men were in the hands of IAS RK Agarwal. As a result, 14 young men from Mansingh's family and relatives paid around 70 lakh rupees in advance to the accused.
Conducted interviews and medical exams in hotels, even showed joining letters
To gain the victims' trust, the accused arranged interviews at two hotels in Jaipur, similar to the movie 'Special-26'. Fake IAS RK Agarwal and Sanjay Meena alias Bunty conducted the interviews. During this time, medical examinations of the young men were also carried out under Sanjay Meena's supervision.
To avoid any doubt, they conducted 2 rounds of interviews in a week. Gang member Rajendra Kumar (Ramlal Meena) posed as a doctor and examined the height, weight and eyes of the youths. The fake doctor also drew blood from the youths in the name of blood tests.
Fraud was revealed when they reached the assembly, phones switched off
According to the fraudsters' promise, on April 11, 2022, Mansingh arrived with his brother at Gate No. 4 of the Assembly to get the joining. However, when he asked the present officials, he was shocked.
The officials present there informed that no such recruitment was ever announced. Upon discovering the fraud, Mansingh contacted the fraudsters. The accused turned off their phones. Following this, Mansingh filed a case against the accused through a complaint on July 2, 2023.
Issued fake letter claiming recruitment under investigation, even created fake investigation committee
When the fraudsters learned about the case, they played another move. The accused sent a fake copy of a Rajasthan Assembly Secretariat order dated February 8, 2022, to the victims' mobile phones. Citing irregularities in clerk grade appointments, the order mentioned the formation of a three-member committee.
This letter was forged in the name of Mahavir Prasad Sharma, Secretary of Rajasthan Legislative Assembly Secretariat. The fraudsters showed IAS RK Agarwal, Ashok Jain and Sunita Meena as members of this committee, so that the matter remains quiet for a few days.
When the police sought information about the record from the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly Secretariat, the Assembly Secretariat denied issuing any such order. The Secretariat informed the police that no such notification has been issued.
Gave false promise of returning money through agreement
Mansingh investigated the accused at his level. On April 20, 2022, he reached their house. Accused Abhishek alias Suneet Sharma and his wife Nisha apologized and promised to return the money through an agreement. After this, on June 5, 2022, other accused also agreed to return the money while apologizing. But as the date approached, they backed out.
Agra transport businessman turned out to be fake IAS
Muralipura in-charge Virendra Kuril said that after the case was registered on July 2, 2023, 3 accused of this gang have been caught so far. Accused Suneet Sharma and Kamal Kishore are still in jail. 3 main accused along with others are absconding.
Fake IAS RK Agarwal was caught from Agra, Uttar Pradesh on March 20. His real name is Deepak Jain (55) and he runs a transport business in Agra. Whenever the accused came to Rajasthan, he met victims and other young men posing as an officer. He is currently in police remand.

title: UP SI Scam 2021: Candidates demand CBI probe into discrepancies; the story so far - Careers360
extracted_title: #UP_SI_Scam_2021: Candidates demand CBI probe into discrepancies; the story so far
article_text:
Top Searches 
Anu Parthiban | March 6, 2024 | 12:32 PM IST | 3 mins read
After 15 trainee inspectors were arrested in Rajasthan for cheating in exam, candidates demand UP Govt to probe 2021 UPSI scam. #UP_SI_2021_Scam is trending on X.
Candidates have once again started X campaign demanding probe on UP SI scam 2021. (Image: X/@varungandhi80)
NEW DELHI: Amid the UP police constable and RO/ARO paper leak allegations, a large section of candidates have started demanding CBI investigation into the Uttar Pradesh sub-inspector recruitment scam that happened in 2021. Several candidates have taken to social media demanding justice and questioned why the Uttar Pradesh government has not investigated the matter yet.
The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board (UPPRPB) held the sub-inspector recruitment exam for 9,534 posts in November 2021. Vivek Kumar, a teacher, was one of the first people to report on the cheating cases to the state police department. He claimed that thousands of candidates who cleared in the UP SI recruitment exam 2021 by cheating are undergoing training now and alleged that it was the biggest recruitment scam worth Rs 500 crore.
Recently, a Special Operations Group (SOG) detained 15 trainee sub-inspectors, including the one who topped the Rajasthan Police recruitment exam 2021, for allegedly using the leaked paper and dummy candidates to clear the exam. Citing the recent development, whistle-blower Vivek Kumar asked “if Rajasthan government can investigate then why not Uttar Pradesh government”. #UP_SI_2021_Scam, #UPSI_SCAM9534, #UPSI_NEEDS_CBI_INVESTIGATION, #UPSI_2021_CBI_INVESTIGATION is trending now on X.
The UPPRPB held the UP sub-inspector recruitment exam from November 21 and December 2 in 2021 to fill 9,534 posts. The UPSI exam was held in computer-based mode due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Nearly 8 lakh candidates appeared in the exam.
Soon after the answer key was published, there were X (formerly Twitter) campaigns demanding the UP police recruitment board to look into the matter as several candidates “who lacked the aptitude to write the exam” had scored 159 marks out of 160.
Initially, over 40 candidates were arrested for using unfair means in the recruitment exam. However, after the results were declared on April 21, it was found that the scam had happened on a large scale and several candidates cleared the exam by cheating, impersonation and paper leak among other unfair means. The investigation was closed after the department arrested over 150 people. Rs 15-25 lakh were reportedly taken from candidates by the solver gang for copying.
It was found that several candidates who scored highest or full marks in the UP SI exam 2021 had completed the exam in minutes. The accused used Virtual Network Computing (VNC), a screen sharing system that was created to remotely control another computer, to attempt the exam.
The state police detained the candidates after checking their Candidate Response Log (CRS). The police said that these candidates had managed to download an application on their examination terminals, which gave the UP SI answers in the last 15 minutes of the exam. This allowed them to finish the exam in minutes, the CNBCTV18 reported.
Over 300 people have been named in it, including more than 30 centre managers from different cities, more than 200 fake candidates, more than 50 solver gang members, cheating mafia, and more than 10 officers and employees of NSEIT companies, Vivek Kumar said.
More than 70 FIRs have been registered so far, however, there is no answer on who gave the contract to the blacklisted company and why a special team was not formed to look into the discrepancies at large.
Notably, the recruitment board had not announced the marks of the all candidates or the topper. Vivek Kumar said “no satisfactory answer” was obtained through RTI regarding the marks secured in the recruitment exams.

Fake Hotel Reviews And Phony Online Jobs: How Scamsters Cheat Netizens
Have you ever visited restaurants or hotels based on online ratings, only to be shocked by their poor or bad service? If so, you might have fallen victim to the 'fake ratings' scam.
Purshottam Joshi from Oneindia Hindi has uncovered an exclusive report on a fake review scam that is prevalent in several parts of the country including in Rajasthan.
Let's delve into the narrative of the fake online ratings on hotels and restaurants. The shocking part of the story reveals that netizens are falling prey to this scam through two distinct avenues. Firstly, people trust these fake ratings to choose hotels and restaurants, only to be disappointed by the actual service. Secondly, a more insidious scam involves unemployed youths who are recruited to provide ratings. They are lured with the promise of easy money, only to be later coerced into investing in the company for its supposed growth.
A multitude of unemployed youths, eager to make a quick buck, find themselves entangled in this web of deceit. Under the false pretence of easy earnings, they are instructed to give ratings to hotels and restaurants, unknowingly contributing to a larger, nefarious plot.
Simultaneously, the masterminds behind the scheme approach these unsuspecting youths with a tempting proposition. After a few successful reviews, they are enticed to invest in the company, promising substantial returns and the opportunity to be part of a growing empire. The web of deception thickens as the lines between genuine reviews and deceit blur.

article_text:
Jammu: The Crime Branch of the Jammu and Kashmir Police has filed a chargesheet against two Punjab residents in connection with an alleged ₹14 lakh fake recruitment scam involving the Military Engineering Services (MES). Investigators said the accused allegedly deceived two job aspirants from Jammu and Kashmir’s Samba district by promising them government jobs, collecting large sums of money, and providing forged appointment letters to keep them convinced that they had been selected. One accused has been arrested, while the other remains absconding. Legal proceedings have been initiated to have the fugitive declared a proclaimed offender.
According to the Crime Branch, the Special Crime Wing (SCW), Jammu, submitted the chargesheet before the Court of the Additional Special Mobile Magistrate in Samba against Bakshish Singh of Amritsar and Amandeep Singh of Jalandhar. The case was registered in 2023 after two residents of Samba alleged that the accused had fraudulently collected ₹14 lakh by falsely assuring them of recruitment into the Military Engineering Services.
The investigation revealed that the accused allegedly portrayed themselves as influential individuals capable of securing appointments in defence establishments. They reportedly assured the victims that their recruitment process had been completed and that they would soon join government service. To make the claims appear genuine, the accused allegedly supplied forged appointment letters and fabricated documents resembling official government recruitment records.
Believing the job offers to be authentic, the victims paid the demanded amount. Police said the accused continued communicating with them, citing various stages of the recruitment process and repeatedly assuring them that their appointments were progressing as planned, thereby preventing the victims from suspecting any wrongdoing.
Investigators said the victims were later instructed to travel to different locations, including Ranchi and Meerut, under the pretext of medical examinations, document verification, and joining formalities. These repeated trips allegedly created the impression that the recruitment process was legitimate. However, subsequent verification with the Military Engineering Services established that the appointment letters were entirely forged and had never been issued by the department.
The Crime Branch stated that the investigation involved the collection of documentary, digital, and financial evidence. Bank transaction records, digital communication data, and forensic examination of the disputed documents corroborated the allegations made by the complainants. Based on these findings, investigators prepared and filed the chargesheet before the court.
Officials said Bakshish Singh was arrested from Amritsar after sustained efforts by the investigating team. However, despite multiple search operations and the issuance of a lookout notice, co-accused Amandeep Singh has remained out of police custody. Authorities have initiated legal proceedings to have him declared a proclaimed offender to facilitate further action under the law.
Investigators said the probe is continuing to determine whether the accused targeted additional victims using similar fraudulent recruitment schemes or were part of a larger organised employment fraud network. The Crime Branch has advised the public to verify every government recruitment offer through the official website or authorised recruitment channels before making any payment and to avoid transferring money to intermediaries claiming to guarantee government jobs.
